 J U D G M E N T

sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation amount of Rs.20,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 28.8.2018 at about 9.15 a.m. the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in a two wheeler bearing No.KA-51-EY- 3851, when she reached near infront of Spring Leaf Hospital, Konappana Agrahara Service Road, Bengaluru, at that time one car bearing No.KA-51-AA- 2015 driven by its driver with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety of others dashed against the motor cycle.

entities.text: Spring Leaf Hospital, Konappana Agrahara Service Road
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Due to the said impact, the petitioner sustained blood stained injuries.
Immediately she was shifted to Sparsha hospital, wherein she was treated as inpatient.

3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy,
aged about 45 years, tailor and earning a sum of Rs.12,000/- per month.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-51-AA-2105.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Contending the above facts, he prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost.
4. In response to the petition notice, the respondents have appeared through their counsel and filed their respective written statement.

5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 are as under:
The respondent No.1 has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of S. 134 and S. 158(6) of the M.V. Act in furnishing the better particulars.
Further contended that driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the same as on the date of accident.
Further contended that driver of the offending vehicle used his car without valid permit and FC at the time of accident.
This respondent has issued a policy of insurance infavour of second respondent in respect of car bearing O.KA-51-AA-2105.
Further contended that the offending vehicle did not involve in the accident as the petitioner has sustained injuries due to fall from the two wheeler bearing NO.KA- 51-EY-3851.
Further contended that the petition is bad for non- joinder of proper and necessary parties to the proceedings.

Further denied the age, avocation and income of the Smt.Chithra R vs Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd on 11 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13780106/
2 petitioner as alleged in the claim petition.

entities.text: Smt.Chithra R vs Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss the claim petition as against this respondent with cost.

6. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under:
The respondent No.2 has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further he has stated that he is the RC owner of the car bearing No.KA-51-AA-2105 and the said car was insured wit the respondent No.1 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Therefore, he is not liable to pay the compensation.

Further denied about the age,
avocation, income of the petitioner and expenses incurred towards medical treatment etc.
Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss the claim petition as against this respondent with cost.

7. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that she had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-51-AA-2105 on 28.8.2018 at about 9.26 a.m. near Konapppanna Agrahara Service Road, infront of Spring Leaf Hospital, Bengaluru ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3. What order or award?
8.
In order to prove the case, the petitioner herself has examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.
9. To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondents have not examined any witness on their behalf.

10. Heard the arguments.
11.

My findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: In the Partly Affirmative Issue No.3:

As per final order for the following:
R E A S O N S 12. ISSUE NO.1:- During the course of arguments, the learned counsel for the petitioner argued by reiterating the contents of petition and also evidence put forth by PW1.

Further he argued that the petitioner has proved his case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary Smt.Chithra R vs Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd on 11 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13780106/
3 evidence.

entities.text: Smt.Chithra R vs Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.

13. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondents have denied the accident in toto, hence,
prays to dismiss the petition.
14. On rival contention urged by both the counsel, I, intend to discuss the merits of the case.
15. In order to prove the case, the petitioner has examined herself as P.W.1 and she has stated in her evidence by reiterating the contents of petition.

Further in support of her evidence, she has produced the prosecution papers and the same are marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P6 such as FIR with complaint, spot mahazar, rough sketch, IMV report wound certificate and charge sheet.
16.
On perusal of Ex.P1 complaint reveals that complaint has been lodged by on Sudhakar on 29.8.2018 and also reasons stated in the complaint for delay in lodging the same.

So, based on the complaint, FIR is registered by Electronic City Traffic Police in Cr. No.27/2018 against the driver of the car for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 337 of IPC and S. 134(B) R/w S. 187 of IMV Act.
Ex.P2 and Ex.P3 spot mahazar and sketch reveals the scene of occurrence.
Ex.P4 is the IMV report reveals that the damages caused to the vehicles and IMV inspector has opined that the accident was not due to any mechanical defect of the vehicle.
Ex.P5 is the wound certificate reveals that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

Ex.P6 is the charge sheet reveals that after investigation I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the car for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 338of IPC and S. 134(B) R/w S. 187 of IMV Act.
17.
The counsel for the respondents argued that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle but not on the part of the driver of the car.
To substantiate the said fact, the respondent has not examined any witness on its behalf nor produced any documents.
On the other hand petitioner has proved her case through oral and documentary evidence.

18. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others).

entities.text: 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 19. Looking to the oral evidence of PW1 and the documents placed before the court, it is clear that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-51-AA-2105.
Hence, I answer this issue in the affirmative.
20. ISSUE NO.2:-
The case of the petitioner is that she met with an accident on 28.8.2018 at about 9.15 a.m. and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately she was shifted to Spring Leaf hospital,
wherein she took the first aid treatment, later on she was shifted to Sparsh Hospital, wherein she was admitted as an inpatient.

To substantiate the said fact, petitioner has produced wound certificate at Ex.P5, which discloses the following injuries:
Fracture of coccyx Smt.Chithra R vs Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd on 11 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13780106/
4 21.
The doctor is of the opinion that the said injury is grievous in nature.

The petitioner has produced copy of the discharge summary marked at Ex.P7, which discloses that petitioner has sustained Coccyx fracture and took the conservative treatment and admitted as inpatient from 28.8.2018 to 30.8.2018.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor.

22. Considering the oral evidence of PW1 and the documents placed before the court, I am of the opinion that the petitioner might have sustained pain and agony, for which, she is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head of pain and sufferings.
23. The case of the petitioner is that, she was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 45 years and working as a tailor and getting an income of Rs.12,000/- per month.
But she has not produced any documents in this regard.
So, considering the present life condition and the age of the petitioner, if notional income of Rs.8,500/- per month is considered, it will meet the ends of justice.

The petitioner has produced copy of the discharge summaries marked at Ex.P7, which discloses that petitioner has sustained coccyx fracture and took the treatment as inpatient from 28.8.2018 to 30.8.2018.
The petitioner has sustained greivous injury, so she might have taken rest and treatment at least for 15 days.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award Rs.4,250/- under the head of loss of income during laid up period and rest period.
24. The contention of the petitioner is that, she has spent huge amount of Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses.

On record she has produced the medical bills marked at Ex.P8 to the extent of Rs.5,221/- and she has also produced final inpatient bill marked at Ex.P10 to the extent of Rs.9,610/- and prescriptions marked at Ex.P9
in total it comes to Rs.14,831/-.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.14,831/- towards medical expenses.
25. Further contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy, aged about 45 years, doing tailoring work and earning Rs.12,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, she is not in a position to walk and not able to do any work.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor to speak about the grievousness of the injuries or to assess the disability.
So, no amount is granted under this head.
26. PW1 has stated that she has sustained grievous injuries and took the treatment as inpatient.
She has produced discharge summary, which is marked at Ex.P7 shows that she took the treatment as inpatient from 28.8.2018 to 30.8.2018.
So, one must attend her during the above said period and she has spent some amount towards conveyance.

Considering the above facts and looking to the period of hospitalization, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.5,000/-
under the head of amenities, attendant, conveyance, food and nourishment etc.

27. Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
 Sl.No. Compensation heads Amount  1. Pain and suffering Rs.20,000-00 2. Loss of income during laid period Rs. 4,250-00 and rest period Smt.Chithra R vs Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd on 11 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13780106/
5

sentences.text: 3. Medical expenses Rs.14,831-00 4. Loss of future income Nil 5. Amenities, Attendant, Rs. 5,000-00
Nourishment and conveyance charges Total Rs.44,081-00 28.
LIABILITY:

On perusal of the contents of petition and contents of written statement, it reveals that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-51-AA-2105.
29.
The respondent No.1 has admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AA-2105 and its validity.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 in partly affirmative.
30. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of above discussion on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of MV act is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.44,081/- with interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of compensation amount together with interest, entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through account payee cheque on proper identification without any further proceedings.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer online, corrected by me and then pronounced in open court on this the 11th day of October 2019).
(MAHANTESH S.DARGAD) III ADDL.SMALL CAUSES JUDGE & ACMM, BANGALORE.
